_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.note: It shows up on lists of things Tesler is credited for, next to the cut, copy and paste he actually did design.

beats.name: Andries van Dam
beats.role: Brown University. His FRESS system is the earliest computer program on record with an undo command, built while Tesler was still an undergraduate, five years before Tesler joined Xerox PARC.

beats.text: It was built at least four times, separately.
beats.note: FRESS in 1968, Warren Teitelman's Programmer's Assistant by 1971, a 1971 doctoral thesis on reversible execution, and Xerox PARC's Bravo editor in 1974, all before Tesler enters the story.

beats.text: In 1980, he fought to keep it.
beats.note: At Apple, he and Bill Atkinson argued to make undo a standard feature of the Lisa. Real influence, just not the invention.

beats.text: Credit followed the more famous name, not the earlier date.

beats.line: Undo has a longer memory than the people who get credit for it.
